clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: 'the effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry be and the same hereby is stayed until July 9, 1934'. Recorded as 1934-07-09, inclusive (the stay runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates; the exclusive alternative ends the stay when July 9, 1934 began. Actor: EO 6743 itself. This is a fixed date before June 14, 1935 and so is the first end; the repeal of June 14, 1935 comes after the stay had run and is not an event of this clause. No held order extends or shortens the stay.

Terminated by statute on June 14, 1935. The clause eliminates the second condition of the approving order (a stay 'until my further order' of an article VII provision), so that 'the provisions of said section shall be ... in full force and effect on the effective date of said code'; it is a modification of an approval under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and the provision it puts in force had effect only as a provision of the approved code. Actor: Congress, S.J. Res. 113, section 2, approved June 14, 1935. Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. No held record shows the baking code cancelled, modified or suspended before June 14, 1935.

Terminated by statute on June 14, 1935. The clause extends the period in which the Code Authority is to report on articles III, IV and V 'to November 15, 1934'. The date is a report deadline, not an end: the deadline passed on November 15, 1934 (functionally spent on that date), but the extension modified the approval order's reporting condition and the Code Authority's duty existed only under the approved code, so the duty's legal basis ended with the repeal. This follows the owner's 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling by analogy: a report-only command does not end on its due date or when the report is made, but when something ends it. research_rationale:
EO 6743 (dated June 16, 1934 in the held text, Franklin D. Roosevelt) modifies the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry and the order of May 28, 1934 approving it, under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6743-modifying-the-code-fair-competition-for-the-baking-industry-and-the.txt, 1,461 characters, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; the transcription contains optical-character errors such as 'hi' for 'in' and 'tlie' for 'the'). APP page check (AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, working-text paragraph): the jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with sha256 60264df5166bf6bd33c72dbf237c46a37988747d9bfc2f264574fc066810fa80 is headed 'Executive Order 6743—Modifying the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry and the Order of Approval Thereof', dated June 16, 1934, node app:node/362518, Common Crawl capture 2025-06-16T14:01:16Z; its text_sha256 bde24fb91473b071f55815d78cfc6157911799116059171c33875ce13083da17 equals the sha256 I computed for the held file, and the page heading, the date and the subject agree with the text. Cotton holds the exact page bytes (jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output/captures). Identity also agrees with the census register row and the WPA 1944 list (page 581: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry modified. XII NRA Codes 247.'). The WPA list dates the order June 15, 1934; the page heading, the census register and the held text all say June 16, 1934. The one-day difference does not change identity (number, subject and the NRA Codes citation agree) and enters no end date below, because every end is keyed to the order's own stated July 9, 1934 or to the June 14, 1935 repeal. The order has three numbered operative clauses, which I have read separately: (1) 'the effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry be and the same hereby is stayed until July 9, 1934'; (2) the second condition of the approving order, which stayed a provision of article VII 'until my further order', 'is hereby eliminated and the provisions of said section shall be ... in full force and effect on the effective date of said code' (the held text reads 'Section G'; the approving order of May 28, 1934, held as a separate APP text, states the stayed provision as 'Section 6', so 'G' is evidently a transcription error for '6'; the lifecycle does not depend on which section); (3) the period in which the Code Authority is to report on the operation and effect of articles III, IV and V 'is hereby extended from the date designated in said order of approval to November 15, 1934'. The machine inventory (three clauses, characters 654 to 789, 791 to 1074 and 1076 to 1426) is complete and correct; the lead-in recital, the 'ORDER NO. 445-2' heading and the signature block command nothing, so no replacement inventory is needed. The dossier's own-terms leads are right for clause 1 (a stated date, July 9, 1934) and clause 3 (a report deadline), and wording matches only for clause 2 ('until my further order' describes the stay that clause 2 removes; clause 2 itself states no period).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searches run on 2026-10-29 over the held texts (clause-drafts copies excluded): (1) every held American Presidency Project order text numbered 6328 to 7074 (904 files), the government printed copies in jobs/hathi-gpo-orders, the Federal Register texts in jobs/fr-originals, and the other held order text folders, for 'Baking Industry', 'baking', 'bakery' and 'bakers'; (2) a citation search of those folders for this order's number in the forms 'Executive Order', 'E.O.', 'Order No.' and 'Orders Nos.'; (3) a scan of the 904 orders numbered 6328 to 7074 for cancel, revoke, supersede, suspend, rescind and terminate wording in orders that mention a code of fair competition or the National Industrial Recovery Act, which reached section 10(b) cancellation of other codes (for example the order cancelling the approval of the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code, December 19, 1934), the service-trades suspension order of May 26, 1934 (which reaches only trades the Administrator later designates, and no held record designates this industry), and stays and terminations of stays in other codes; none names this code or this order. The machine searches of the U.S. Code and eCFR (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. The only held orders naming the baking code are the approving order of May 28, 1934 (EO 6725-A, whose government printed copy is not held; the number 6725 in the government printed volume belongs to an unrelated Science Advisory Board order) and this order. No held record shows this code cancelled, modified under section 10(b), superseded, suspended or stayed before June 14, 1935. Later orders that act on Title I generally, of June 15, 1935 (the reorganization of the NRA and the order extending Title I activities to April 1, 1936 'so far as consistent' with Title I as amended, whose proviso disclaims any authority to approve or prescribe codes or to provide for their enforcement), post-date the repeal and do not continue a code approval. Amendments are later events, not ends; June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Clause 1 has an own-terms end before June 14, 1935 (July 9, 1934), which is its first end. For clauses 2 and 3 no earlier end is held; in particular nothing held modifies, stays or cancels the modification after June 16, 1934.","independent_command_check":"None of the three clauses is independent of the code. Clause 1 stays the code's own effective date; clause 2 lifts a condition of the approval of the code; clause 3 adjusts the reporting duty of the Code Authority, a body that exists only under the approved code (the approving order imposes the report). The order makes no appointment, creates no committee or board, delegates nothing under another statute and directs no agency, and no clause here is a stay 'pending further order' (clause 2 removes one), so no independent command is retained and the order is not a mixed order.","savings_check":"Clause 1: once the stay ran through July 9, 1934 the code's effective date arrived and the code took effect; that is a completed effect of the stay and keeps nothing of the stay operative. Clauses 2 and 3: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.","scope_check":"Three separate commands, each given its own end: a stay of the code's effective date to a fixed date (clause 1), the removal of a condition that stayed one provision of the approval (clause 2), and the extension of a reporting date for the Code Authority (clause 3). Clause 1 is a stay to a fixed date before June 14, 1935, so its own-terms end controls. The extension in clause 3 moves a deadline: a report deadline is not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadlines), so the November 15, 1934 date is recorded as a spent fact, 'functionally spent on November 15, 1934', and the clause's end is the repeal that removed the approval the Code Authority's duty rested on; no held record shows whether the Code Authority reported by that date. No partial event inside any clause is held or found."}

savings.reason: Clause 1: once the stay ran through July 9, 1934 the code's effective date arrived and the code took effect; that is a completed effect of the stay and keeps nothing of the stay operative. Clauses 2 and 3: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date.
source_notes.reason: Schechter judgment: the code provisions in question held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground; recorded as a validity characterization of approvals under section 3, not as an end of this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: date of the original enactment; supplies the content of the repealed provisions, not an end date.
source_notes.reason: Section 3(a)-(f): the approval power and the legal effects that flowed only from an approved code (standards of fair competition, equity jurisdiction, misdemeanor); these are the effects the June 14, 1935 repeal removed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-06-16: original two-year expiry under section 2(c), replaced by April 1, 1936; not an end date.
source_notes.reason: Section 2(c) set Title I's original two-year expiry; section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced it with April 1, 1936, so the original expiry date is not an end of this approval.
